findings: Disposition of a1 control/backtick recommendation (advisory limitation, not a mandatory change): In crates/mori/src/commands/init.rs:106-111, std::env::current_exe() is validated as UTF-8 via to_str() and single-quoted (`format!("'{}'", executable.replace('\'', "'\\''"))`) before std::fs::create_dir(&args.dir) (line 114). In POSIX sh, single quotes suppress all expansion (including backticks, `$`, globs, and word splitting); args.dir is never interpolated into README.md, and action is a closed match ("pay"|"repay", lines 52-55). Because current_exe() is the caller's own binary path rather than untrusted input, unrejected control/backtick characters in current_exe() are an advisory Markdown presentation limitation only.

Disposition of a1 non-UTF-8 path coverage recommendation (advisory test-coverage limitation, not a mandatory change): Production crates/mori/src/commands/init.rs:107-109 (`executable.to_str().ok_or_else(|| super::core_io::operation("starter commands require a UTF-8 Rust executable path"))?`) is unchanged (SHA256 e7640559...), refuses non-UTF-8 executable paths without lossy substitution before std::fs::create_dir(&args.dir) (line 114), and sanitizes diagnostics via crate::display::text (core_io.rs:161). While crates/mori/tests/init.rs:344 tests valid UTF-8 ("Rust CLI's tools 🧪") rather than non-UTF-8 OsStr, the 3-line guard is directly inspectable; extracting a unit-test helper is advisory only.

A2 test delta (proposal/a1-to-a2.patch, tests/init.rs SHA256 26a616f9...) replaces hardcoded `/bin/sh` with host PATH resolution in crates/mori/tests/init.rs:328-342,365, achieving literal compliance with RUST_GUIDELINES.md:59 (`No absolute paths.`) without a guideline exception. Before clearing child PATH, the test walks std::env::var_os("PATH") via std::env::split_paths, selects the first `sh` where fs::metadata is a file with mode `& 0o111 != 0`, and canonicalizes it via fs::canonicalize before `.current_dir(&dir)` and `.env("PATH", "")` (lines 351-352, 366-367). Both `mori init` and the child shell still execute with `PATH=""`, proving README commands run the creating Rust CLI without PATH lookup.

Public CLI consumer fidelity and manifest boundaries match across crates/mori/src/commands/init.rs:50-101 and crates/mori/src/commands/{mod,check,simulate,test}.rs. Generated README commands invoke `check source.mori --json` (check.rs:29-60 -> status=accepted, language=moriarty/1), `simulate source.mori --action {action} --scenario scenario.json` (simulate.rs:109-147 -> qualification=local-reference-execution, execution.semantics=moriarty-core/1), and `test .` (test.rs:39-89 -> profile=moriarty-tests/1, full post/effects check). Under crates/mori/Cargo.toml:10-25,64-107 and mori-core/Cargo.toml:8-25, `tests/init.rs` needs no `native` feature and fits the CLI binary-test rule (RUST_GUIDELINES.md:253-256).

Portability boundary in crates/mori/src/commands/init.rs:93,106-110 and crates/mori/tests/init.rs:325-395: README.md embeds the creating binary's runtime path in POSIX single quotes, explicitly scopes usage to "in a POSIX shell" (line 93), and notes the path must be updated if the executable moves. On Windows, current_exe() single-quoted paths work in POSIX shells (e.g. Git Bash) but not directly in cmd.exe/PowerShell without `&`. In tests/init.rs:325-342, `generated_commands_use_the_creating_rust_cli_without_path_lookup` is `#[cfg(unix)]` and requires the test host's initial `PATH` to contain an executable `sh` file resolvable by `fs::canonicalize`.

As designated security fallback, the remaining a1 recommendations—filtering control/backtick characters in current_exe() and unit-testing the non-UTF-8 OsStr error branch—are explicitly disposed as advisory limitations, not mandatory source changes.
